unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee of a covered employer qualifies as an eligible employee for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.choice_text: An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees); AND (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (subject to § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the break-in-service provisions.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the rules governing breaks in service are satisfied.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, for employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years where either a USERRA service obligation or a written rehire agreement applies.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (such as for education or childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when an employee is absent from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Regarding employee entitlements under 29 CFR 825.110 in relation to USERRA.
unit_attributes.statement: This section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining duration of employment, if an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (such as sick or vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees, in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785), with the determining factor being the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is not limited by methods of recordkeeping, or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all of the hours an employee has worked for or been in service to the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service (subject to special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).
unit_attributes.statement: In determining an employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, an employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, and accordingly has the hours that would have been worked added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement (subject to special rules in § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (subject to special rules in § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's recordkeeping requirements (such as bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked and claims that full-time teachers of an educational establishment who often work outside the classroom or at home are not eligible for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: must be able to clearly demonstrate
unit_attributes.statement: In order to claim that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment are not eligible for FMLA leave when accurate records are not kept, an employer must be able to clearly demonstrate that the teachers did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start (referencing § 825.300(b) for eligibility notice rules).

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement is FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In ascertaining an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles of the worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether leave is taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave while the employer employs 50 or more employees within 75 miles, even if the employer expects the number of employees to drop below 50 by the time the leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles (such as 60 employees in August), even if the employer expects the number of employees to drop below 50 (such as to 40 in December) for a period of leave to begin in December.
